title: Claude for Creative Work
verification: Primary official announcement; capabilities are described by the vendor, not independently benchmarked.
claim: Blender MCP is an officially available natural-language interface to Blender Python API and documentation; intended uses include scene analysis, scripts, plugins, procedural animation, parametric models and batch work.
agent_use: Confirms that API-driven Blender assistance is a legitimate workflow, but does not prove expert modeling quality.
adopted: Yes: semantic API, scripting, tutoring and repetitive-task positioning.

title: ahujasid/blender-mcp
verification: Public source code and observable repository activity; README claims are maintainer-authored.
claim: Socket-based MCP bridge, scene inspection, screenshots, object/material control, arbitrary Blender Python execution, asset-service integrations; roughly 23k stars and 2.3k forks at snapshot.
agent_use: Strong popularity and implementation reference. Use one server instance, explicit health checks, privacy settings, and semantic wrappers; popularity is not proof of modeling fidelity.
adopted: Existing connection retained; no replacement bundled. Added optional Python pin/telemetry/one-instance hardening guidance.

title: Blender MCP commands timeout on Windows 11 with Blender 5.1
verification: Concrete user report with environment and logs; not a controlled benchmark.
claim: Connection can appear active while tool calls time out on Blender 5.1.
agent_use: Requires health checks, structured timeouts and retry/abort semantics.
adopted: Yes: compatibility probe and failure policy.

title: Incomplete JSON response, MCP timeout
verification: Concrete logs; single-user report.
claim: Long waits and truncated/incomplete JSON can break scene inspection.
agent_use: Do not retry blindly; use bounded retries and idempotent operations.
adopted: Yes: structured error categories in staged state.

title: Arbitrary File Read via generate_hunyuan3d_model
verification: Detailed reproducible vulnerability report; issue later closed as completed.
claim: Unvalidated local paths in an external-generation tool enabled arbitrary readable files to be encoded and sent to an API.
agent_use: Local path allowlisting and network-off-by-default are required.
adopted: Yes: security preflight and path policy; not claimed as a complete sandbox.

title: Vision-as-Inverse-Graphics Agent via Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning (VIGA)
verification: Detailed method, benchmark and ablations; preprint and primarily author-evaluated.
claim: Code-render-inspect loop, high-level semantic skills, strict observation/modification separation and bounded multimodal memory improve long-horizon graphics work.
agent_use: Directly supports read-only inspection tools, short memory and targeted edits.
adopted: Yes: core v4 architecture.

title: Thinking in Blender: Staged Executable Inverse Graphics with Vision-Language Models
verification: Method, experiments and limitations are explicit; very recent preprint without broad independent replication.
claim: Separate geometry, material, composition and lighting stages; use a scoped verifier and explicit approval checklist for each stage.
agent_use: Prevents material edits from damaging geometry and reduces cross-stage confusion.
adopted: Yes: stage permissions, budgets, commits and optional global review.

title: BlenderGym: Benchmarking Foundational Model Systems for Graphics Editing
verification: 245 task instances, human baselines and verifier study; preprint.
claim: Current VLM systems lag human Blender users; API mismatch, non-executable scripts and unreliable visual verifiers remain major failure modes.
agent_use: Use compatibility tests, multiple views, structural QA and occasional human A/B choice rather than one visual metric.
adopted: Yes: candidate selection and non-visual QA.

title: 3DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agentic Procedural 3D Modeling Via Code
verification: Large benchmark and human preference arena; very recent preprint.
claim: Failures mostly come from API mismatches; even successful renders may contain disconnected or floating components; more reasoning and multi-turn refinement help.
agent_use: Adds version probes, connection graph checks and a refinement budget.
adopted: Yes: compatibility and assembly QA.

title: BlenderRAG: High-Fidelity 3D Object Generation via Retrieval-Augmented Code Synthesis
verification: 500 expert-validated examples and reported ablations; author-reported results, young public codebase.
claim: Retrieving similar text/code/image examples improved reported compilation success and semantic similarity without fine-tuning.
agent_use: Store compact verified examples and retrieve only top matches.
adopted: Yes: dependency-free local example index; external vector DB remains optional.

title: MaxRondelli/BlenderRAG
verification: Public code; around 12 stars, 1 fork and 41 commits at snapshot.
claim: Implements local retrieval with a vector database and executes generated scripts in Blender.
agent_use: Useful implementation reference, but adoption is currently small.
adopted: Concept only; no Qdrant dependency bundled.

title: LL3M: Large Language 3D Modelers
verification: Research system with examples and experiments; preprint.
claim: Specialized agents plan, retrieve, write, debug and refine interpretable Blender Python using bmesh, modifiers and shader nodes.
agent_use: Supports role separation and editable procedural code.
adopted: Partially: planner/executor/reviewer roles, not a large permanent agent swarm.

title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scene as Blender Code
verification: Method and evaluation; preprint.
claim: A scene graph, numerical spatial constraints, render feedback and a reusable function library support complex scenes with many assets.
agent_use: Create a scene graph before code and learn reusable functions rather than memorizing chat.
adopted: Yes: scene graph schema and reusable example records.

title: 3D-GPT: Procedural 3D Modeling with Large Language Models
verification: Early research prototype; older model generation and limited modern MCP relevance.
claim: Task dispatch, conceptualization and modeling agents can decompose procedural modeling tasks.
agent_use: Supports simple role decomposition.
adopted: Concept only; kept to three logical roles, not separate always-on agents.

title: From Idea to Co-Creation: A Planner-Actor-Critic Framework for Agent Augmented 3D Modeling
verification: Systematic comparison claimed, but limited independent replication and recent preprint.
claim: Planner-Actor-Critic with human supervision outperforms a direct single-prompt workflow in reported geometry, aesthetics and task completion.
agent_use: Give critic a checklist and allow user approval at ambiguous decisions.
adopted: Yes: lightweight roles and human checkpoint, not conversational bureaucracy.

title: 3Dify: Procedural 3D-CG Generation Assisted by LLMs Using MCP and RAG
verification: Research proposal and system description; limited independent validation.
claim: MCP + RAG + user selection among candidates can reuse preferred parameter patterns; local LLMs are possible.
agent_use: Keep a small preference log and generate alternatives only where uncertainty is high.
adopted: Yes: optional A/B candidate records.

title: Proc3D: Procedural 3D Generation and Parametric Editing
verification: Author-reported benchmarks; representation differs from this kit.
claim: A compact procedural graph with exposed parameters enables fast edits without regenerating the whole object.
agent_use: Prefer editable parameters, named parts and modifier stacks over destructive final meshes.
adopted: Yes: parametric representation policy.

title: Blendify — Python rendering framework for Blender
verification: Public framework and technical report; focused more on rendering than modeling.
claim: A high-level API reduces native Blender API complexity for scene creation, colors, materials and rendering.
agent_use: Supports semantic wrappers instead of raw bpy everywhere.
adopted: Already aligned with toolkit design.

title: EZBlender: Efficient 3D Editing with Plan-and-ReAct Agent
verification: Research benchmark and claims; recent preprint.
claim: Global planning plus reactive local autonomy can reduce latency/cost while preserving editing quality.
agent_use: Plan once, then use small local corrections rather than replanning the whole project.
adopted: Yes: stage plan plus targeted attempt loop.

title: Blender MCP Assembly Skill
verification: Open instructions and before/after example; around 30 stars at snapshot; no large benchmark.
claim: Connection planning, world-space bounds, overlap checks, transform application and final audits reduce disconnected assemblies.
agent_use: Directly addresses floating fingers, tubes, chair parts and mascot components.
adopted: Yes: independently implemented structural audit and connection graph.

title: Blender MCP + AI AGNO Multi-Agent Production Studio
verification: Open code and README; about 48 stars; demo link remains a placeholder in README.
claim: Proposes 17 specialized agents and persistent memory across a full production pipeline.
agent_use: Shows specialization is feasible, but does not establish that 17 agents are efficient or necessary.
adopted: No: rejected as default due to context, cost and orchestration overhead.

title: saofund/LLM-Blender-Agent
verification: Public code; about 29 stars, 6 forks and 56 commits at snapshot.
claim: Supports multiple LLM providers, function calling, Gradio, assets and external text/image-to-3D services.
agent_use: Useful connector/provider reference; external generators do not replace editable procedural modeling.
adopted: No external model services bundled.

title: sandraschi/blender-mcp
verification: Public code with tests and 108 commits; about 14 stars at snapshot.
claim: A broader tool suite can support headless/live Blender, exports, VSE, geometry nodes and other workflows.
agent_use: Shows headless testing and explicit tool families are practical.
adopted: Concept only; no replacement server bundled.

title: 3D Agent for Blender
verification: Marketing claims and selected testimonials; no independent benchmark located.
claim: Claims broad model support and faster creation workflows.
agent_use: Demonstrates market interest, not proof of reliable expert-grade output.
adopted: No vendor code or claims imported.

title: Community discussion of AI-driven Blender modeling
verification: Anecdotal community discussion; identities, setups and success criteria vary.
claim: Users describe fast concept/blockout gains but acknowledge organic sculpting, precise CAD and polished characters remain difficult.
agent_use: Sets realistic expectations: strong for structured blockout and iteration, weak as autonomous master sculptor.
adopted: Yes: scope boundaries documented.

title: Reddit feedback: Blender MCP / Claude modeling
verification: Anecdotal, self-selected reports; often missing exact prompts, versions and output files.
claim: Positive reports emphasize editable low-poly props and automation; negative reports mention poor spatial reasoning, primitive-looking objects and slow iteration.
agent_use: Explains why reproducible logs, versions, references and acceptance tests matter.
adopted: Feedback informs failure taxonomy only.

title: AI Agent Creates 3D Models in Blender from Text (MCP Tutorial)
verification: Linked by the main repository; video is a demonstration, not a controlled evaluation.
claim: Shows installation and prompt-driven Blender operations.
agent_use: Useful for setup and interaction patterns; convert only verified steps into skills.
adopted: Indexed, not transcribed or treated as training data.

title: Blender MCP setup instruction video
verification: Linked by repository installation documentation.
claim: Demonstrates connector setup.
agent_use: Installation only; no evidence of complex modeling competence.
adopted: Indexed for human setup.

title: Blender MCP Assembly Skill tutorial
verification: Linked from an open skill repository with inspectable instructions.
claim: Explains connection planning, bounds, overlap and transform auditing.
agent_use: Good candidate for converting video lessons into explicit checks.
adopted: Concept reproduced independently in v4 structural QA.

title: Blender Python API Documentation
verification: Primary API reference; version-specific behavior still needs runtime probing.
claim: Authoritative source for bpy, bmesh, types, operators and version data.
agent_use: Use API docs plus capability probes; do not trust remembered signatures.
adopted: Yes: version/capability probe and source priority.

title: Model Context Protocol documentation
verification: Primary protocol documentation.
claim: MCP standardizes discovery and invocation of tools/resources; it does not itself teach Blender artistry or guarantee safe execution.
agent_use: Treat MCP as transport/tool contract, not skill memory.
adopted: Yes: architecture distinction.

title: Bridging Protocol and Production: Design Patterns for Deploying AI Agents with MCP
verification: Field-informed design paper; enterprise client and some details are redacted.
claim: Reliable production MCP needs explicit timeouts, structured errors, tool budgets, identity/context and observability beyond protocol basics.
agent_use: Add deterministic error classes, budgets and logs.
adopted: Yes: attempt limits and machine-readable stage failures.
